# Every Claude session you have running, on one small board.

Clowder is a native Mac status board for AI coding sessions. Each one is a coloured tile: red has stopped and needs you, green has finished, blue is still working. One glance and you know where to go.

Free for ever, four tiles. macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon.

- Needs you

- Ready

- Working

- Idle, active lately

- Idle, long dormant

The problem

## An agent that finishes quietly has stopped working for you.

Run eight or thirteen Claude sessions across as many worktrees and the difficult part is no longer the work. It is the bookkeeping.

One has stopped to ask whether it may run a command, and will happily wait all afternoon for an answer. Another finished four minutes ago and is just sitting there holding the result. Neither says a word, so off you go looking â a terminal window here, VS Code there, the Claude app behind both â and of course the one you checked last is the one that was waiting.

Clowder is the bit that tells you. Keep it floating in a corner of the screen, or skip the window altogether and keep a row of small squares in the menu bar. Either way it does one thing: when something wants you, you know in seconds rather than a quarter of an hour later.

The five states

## Each colour says what the session wants from you.

It is a traffic light for your attention, not for the machine's. Green means go and look, which is why a working session is blue: it wants nothing from you, and giving it the ready colour made the whole board look like it needed attention.

### Colour is never the only signal

Urgency comes through brightness and movement first, colour second, because that is what you catch out of the corner of your eye. Every state also has its own mark and its own bar thickness, so you are never relying on telling two colours apart.

### Age is the triage signal

Each tile shows how long it has been in its state, because a prompt open fourteen minutes matters more than one open five seconds. The board sorts on that: state first, then whatever has been waiting on you longest.

What it reads

## Five sources, all of them on this Mac.

Clowder watches the files Claude already writes on your own machine. There is no account to make, no sign-in, and nothing is sent anywhere.

- Claude Code in the terminal, your editor, anywhere it runs

- Code in the Claude app the Code tab, including remote sessions

- Claude Cowork in the Claude app

- Claude Design designs in the Claude app

- Claude chats ordinary conversations you have touched lately

### Switch on the ones you want

All five work, and all five are in daily use here. You turn each one on in Settings, so your board shows the kinds of work you actually do rather than everything at once.

One honest note. Claude Code announces what it is doing, so those tiles are always right. The other four are read from the Claude app's own files on your Mac, and Claude changes those from time to time without telling anyone. If a source ever goes quiet, that is usually why â and the fix tends to arrive the same day, because this is a small app with one person watching it.

Built for a glance

## A board you can act from, not just read.

### Click a tile, land in the session

Not the app â the session itself. The right conversation in the Claude app, whether it lives under Chat or under Code. The right tab in VS Code. The right terminal window. With a dozen windows open, bringing an application to the front barely helps; Clowder brings the one you wanted. It only ever raises something already running â it will not open anything for you.

### It comes and finds you

The moment a session needs you, its tile hops â once, three times, five, or not at all, whichever you prefer. The Dock icon shows the same picture, and so does the row of small squares in the menu bar, for when the board is buried behind something.

### Arranged how you want it

Tiles sort themselves by what is most urgent, so the thing shouting loudest is always top left. If you would rather a particular session stayed put, drag it where you want it and pin it there. Rename anything to a name you will actually recognise, and hide a session â or a whole project â you would rather not see.

### Out of the way until it isn't

It floats above your other windows, so it is still there whatever you are working in. Fade it back as far as you like and it will turn solid again the moment your pointer lands on it. Drag a corner or pinch to resize, anywhere from a full wall of tiles down to a thin strip of coloured chips tucked in the corner of the screen.

### Or no window at all

Clowder can live entirely in the menu bar, with no board and no Dock icon. Click the squares and every session is listed with its state and how long it has been in it; click one to jump straight there. Hold â¥ and each row becomes a menu â rename, pin, hide, or move it to a different square â so the whole app works without the board ever being on screen.

### As far back as you want

Claude keeps conversations for weeks, so a session earns a tile by having been touched recently rather than by merely existing. That window is yours to set: today, three days, a week, or everything Clowder can see.
